learning_question: On the frozen screen's output in the survivorship-free S&P 500 replay, which selection rule, core exit rule, and trade-plan tactical variant gives the highest probability (lower confidence bound) of beating a plain value book (the hsr-v1 earnings-yield sort, equal weight, monthly, same costs) over 36 months? Does holding the core until a thesis break (PR #1021) beat selling on leaving the selection, and does a re-rating exit bound open-ended holding without giving that up? Does the tactical slice add to the core once its idle cash and costs are counted?
inputs: The hsr-v1 build (ftse-historical-replay build-panel): panel.csv.gz, daily.csv.gz (adjusted daily OHLC), terminal_baseline.csv, and the screen signals cached by the replay. All outside the repository.

holdout.reveal_rule: Revealed once, after the search selection is committed and nothing in this file has changed. Later reveals are exploratory.

grid.size: 2 tiers x 3 top_n x 5 exit rules x (27 tactical variants + core only) = 840 rule sets

objective.definition: P(cumulative monthly log excess over the plain value book, summed over H months, > 0) = Phi(mu * sqrt(H) / sigma_LR), sigma_LR the Newey-West long-run standard deviation. p_lower replaces mu with mu - z * sigma_LR / sqrt(T). The empirical overlapping H-month hit rate is reported beside it, not optimised. The plain value book holds the top 30% by positive earnings yield of the screened names, equal weight, rebalanced monthly, charged the same cost per side on its turnover; a month with no such names uses the equal-weight universe and is counted. PBO and the deflated Sharpe use the same excess series.
objective.market_context: The same probability against the cap-weighted screened universe, excess over the cap- and equal-weighted universes, and the plain book's own excess over the cap-weighted universe (the value regime) are reported per rule set. They do not enter selection or verdicts.

selection_rule: Score every rule set on the development window only. Choose the highest plateau score: the median objective over the rule set and its one-step neighbours in each grid dimension. Ties go to core only, then to the fewest departures from frozen_config. Report the probability of backtest overfitting (CSCV) across all rule sets and the deflated Sharpe ratio of the chosen set.
reveal_order: Commit docs/data/historical_rule_search.json with the selection before any holdout reveal, including hsr-v1's (ftse-historical-replay run --reveal-holdout refuses until then). Reveal hrs-v1 once: frozen and chosen, each with and without the tactical slice, at base and stress costs.

costs.model: Core: cost x one-way turnover at each monthly rebalance. Slice: cost on each fill and each exit, plus cost on monthly resizing while the slice is in position.
costs.source: Base is the fair S&P 500 cost for this GBP-funded investor from market_trading_costs (sp500, t212_invest_fair_v1): about 0.15% FX per conversion plus a 0.025% half-spread, 0.175% per side. Stress is 3% per side.

pass_bars.tactical_verdict: adds when the holdout 95% interval of (combined minus core-only) monthly return is wholly above zero; costs when wholly below; otherwise inconclusive.
pass_bars.chosen_vs_frozen: chosen beats frozen when the holdout 95% interval of the paired monthly difference (chosen minus frozen, same months) is wholly above zero at base cost.
pass_bars.verdict_vs_plain_value: pass when the holdout 36-month p_lower against the plain value book >= 0.5 at base cost; fail when p < 0.5; otherwise inconclusive.
pass_bars.market_context_vs_cap_weighted: The same rule against the cap-weighted universe, reported as context only.

simplifications: The core enters and exits at the month-end close, also when the live plan would place a core limit order.
Monthly re-equalisation restores each name's core : slice split from the plan active at entry.
Plans are rebuilt on the last trading day of each ISO week (live recomputes on every screen run); a plan stays live until the next weekly date.
Within a day the stop is checked before the target; gaps fill at the open; no exit on the fill day; no fill on the core's exit day.
After a slice exit it re-arms only on a newer plan, so one holding can run several buy/sell cycles.
Benchmarks come from the screened panel universe (S&P 500 members with fundamentals): the plain value book decides; cap-weighted and equal-weighted returns are context.
Exit rules run on monthly screens; the live rules confirm on weekly screens.
fixed_rules: The screen (assign_signal thresholds, model weights, scoring) is frozen and not searched (N33). Only rules applied after the screen are in the grid.
No grid point, metric, horizon, or window changes after the search runs; changes open a new registration_id.
Only config-level aggregates are committed. Signals, panels, prices and per-name trades stay with the licensed build outside the repository.

decisions.chosen_passes_and_beats_frozen: Chosen passes verdict_vs_plain_value and chosen_minus_frozen is 'adds': propose the chosen selection and tactical variant as a cold-start paper twin (L572 path) with a frozen epoch; no live book changes on backtest evidence alone.
decisions.frozen_passes_chosen_does_not: Keep the live rules; the search found noise.
decisions.tactical_costs_or_inconclusive: Treat the tactical slice as unproven: keep alerts only and do not build a cycling slice into paper books until a forward twin shows an increment.
decisions.neither_passes: Neither rule set beats the plain value book: the selection rules add nothing over textbook value; follow the hsr-v1 decision.
decisions.patient_exit_chosen: If the chosen rule set uses rerate or thesis and passes the holdout, propose that exit for the core sell trigger (core_sell_trigger.py) through a cold-start twin; the replayed thresholds are the starting values, not a live edit.
decisions.chosen_not_better_than_frozen: chosen_minus_frozen is inconclusive or costs: the search did not beat the live rules out of sample; keep them.
decisions.market_context: Market-relative results are read beside the verdicts with the plain book's own excess (the value regime). Lagging the market while beating the plain book is a value-regime result, not a rule failure.

exit_rules.order: Ordered from quickest to most patient sell; the plateau steps along this order.

definitions.tier: Sell after screens_outside monthly screens outside the selection; a single avoid sells at once (the live buy_tier_level rule; 2 weekly confirm screens are closest to 1 monthly screen).
definitions.thesis: The PR #1021 core sell trigger, screen leg only: leaving the selection is not a sell; sell after avoid_confirm consecutive avoid screens. The research-verdict leg (pass/sell/avoid/exit) cannot be replayed (N39), so the replay sells less often than the live rule would.
definitions.rerate: thesis plus a valuation exit: sell after rerate_confirm consecutive screens outside the selection with the earnings yield below rerate_below_pct of the names screened that date (re-rated: no longer cheap). A missing earnings yield leaves the streak unchanged.
definitions.all_rules: A name that leaves the screened universe (left the S&P 500, or no price within 7 days) is sold at that month-end: no later screen could confirm a sell. Counted as left_universe.

reporting: Per rule set and window: holding-period median, 90th percentile and maximum in months, episodes still open at the window end, and sells by reason (avoid, left_selection, thesis_break, rerated, left_universe).

amendments.reason: The holdout decade favoured growth; a market benchmark would mostly score the value regime, which no selection or exit rule controls. A plain value book shares that regime, so the search ranks rules on what they add to value. No search has run and no holdout has been revealed.
